chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Rabah al-Qalla', who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام about a man whose brother died and left a صندوق containing pledged items. Some of them had the name of their owner on them and the amount for which they had been pledged, while some of them it was not known whose they were, nor for how much they had been pledged. What do you say regarding this whose owner is not known?
So he عليه السلام said: 'It is like the rest of his property.'

key_terms.رُهُونٌ: pledged items or collateral held against a debt
key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: its owner, the person to whom the item belongs
key_terms.صُنْدُوقًا: a box or chest containing property
key_terms.كَمَالِهِ: like the rest of his property or estate
key_terms.لَا يُعْرَفُ: is not known or cannot be identified

ai.seo_question: How are unidentified pledged items in a deceased person's possession treated in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about pledged property left behind by a deceased person when some items cannot be identified by owner or value. The Imam عليه السلام states that such unknown items are treated as part of the deceased's estate, making the report relevant to financial law, trust, and the rights attached to property.
